To manage the analysis across multiple bioRxiv subjects, the [`process_all_subjects.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/DETAILS.md#L86) script at [`/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/process_all_subjects.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/process_all_subjects.py) acts as an orchestrator. It parses arguments to configure parameters such as the number of papers per subject, output paths, and LLM model. This script verifies the availability of papers for specified subjects and then iteratively calls [`extract_biorxiv_tasks.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/DETAILS.md#L84) for each subject. After individual subject processing is complete, [`combine_summaries`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/process_all_subjects.py#L199) aggregates the frequency summaries generated for each subject into a global [`combined_summary.json`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/process_all_subjects.py#L261) and separate CSV files, providing a consolidated view of tasks, databases, and software across all analyzed subjects.

Further leveraging the insights gained from task extraction, the [`generate_function.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/DETAILS.md#L85) script at [`/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/generate_function.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/biorxiv_scripts/generate_function.py) facilitates the automatic generation of Python functions from JSON-defined task descriptions. This script takes a JSON file containing task descriptions, uses an LLM-powered [`FunctionGenerator`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/function_generator.py#L22) agent to convert these descriptions into executable Python code, and saves the generated code to a specified output directory. This capability allows the system to not only identify research tasks but also to automatically create computational tools to address them.

## Tutorials and Examples
The [`biomni`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/README.md#L25) framework provides practical examples and tutorials to guide users in applying its capabilities to biomedical problems. These resources demonstrate how to work with biological sequence data and illustrate the setup, execution, and testing of a Multi-Component Protocol (MCP) server.

One area of focus is handling raw biological sequence data. For instance, the file [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/plentiCRISPR.txt`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/plentiCRISPR.txt) contains DNA nucleotides that can serve as input for various bioinformatics tools within the [`biomni`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/README.md#L25) framework. This provides a tangible example for users to understand how external data can be integrated into the system for analysis.

Another practical demonstration involves the operation of a Biomni MCP server. The [`run_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/docs/mcp_integration.md#L268) script, located in [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/run_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/run_mcp_server.py), shows how to initialize and run such a server. This server is configured to expose database-related [`tool_modules`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1995) and uses standard I/O for communication. Complementing this, the [`test_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/docs/mcp_integration.md#L211) script in [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py) acts as a client. It connects to the running MCP server, lists the available tools, and demonstrates how to invoke a specified tool with provided arguments, subsequently parsing and displaying the results. This setup illustrates the client-server interaction model and the process of tool discovery and execution within the [`biomni`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/README.md#L25) ecosystem.

### Working with Biological Sequence Data
The [`biomni`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/README.md#L25) framework facilitates the handling and utilization of raw biological sequence data for various bioinformatics tools. An example of such data is provided in the file [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/plentiCRISPR.txt`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/plentiCRISPR.txt). This file contains a raw sequence of nucleotides, typically DNA (composed of 'A', 'C', 'G', 'T'), which can serve as input for further analysis within the system. This type of raw data is fundamental for various bioinformatics tasks, including sequence alignment, gene prediction, or primer design, which can then be processed by the comprehensive suite of [Biomedical Tools and Resources](#biomedical-tools-and-resources) available in [`biomni`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/README.md#L25).

### Setting up and Running a Multi-Component Protocol (MCP) Server
The Biomni framework includes a tutorial for setting up and running a Multi-Component Protocol (MCP) server, located in [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server). This example demonstrates how to initialize and execute a Biomni MCP server, configuring it with specific tool modules and utilizing [`stdio`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L378) for its transport mechanism.

The core of the server setup is handled by the script [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/run_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/run_mcp_server.py). This script instantiates an agent using the [`A1`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L56) class and then creates an MCP server. The server is configured to expose a set of database-related functionalities through [`biomni.tool.database`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/DETAILS.md#L324) [`tool_modules`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L1995). This setup allows the server to offer specialized biomedical tools as services. For instance, the script configures the server to use [`stdio`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L378) as its communication transport, which facilitates interaction with client applications via standard input/output streams. The server, once initialized, runs to provide access to its exposed tools.

### Testing Exposed Tools of an MCP Server
The [`test_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/docs/mcp_integration.md#L211) script in [`/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py) provides a client-side mechanism for validating the functionality of individual tools exposed by a Biomni Multi-Component Protocol (MCP) server. This script connects to a local server instance (typically launched by [`run_mcp_server.py`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/docs/mcp_integration.md#L268) in the same directory) via standard input/output (stdio) and performs a series of actions to test a designated tool.

The testing process begins by establishing a connection to the server. The client then discovers the tools available on the server by listing them. Once a [`target_tool`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py#L70) is identified (configured via the [`TOOL_TO_TEST`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py#L14) constant), the script displays its key characteristics, including its name, description, and the schema of its input parameters. Subsequently, the script invokes this tool using predefined arguments ([`TEST_ARGS`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/tutorials/examples/expose_biomni_server/test_mcp_server.py#L15)) and processes the result. Results are typically expected in JSON format, which the script parses and displays in a structured manner. The script also incorporates robust error handling, providing informative messages and suggestions, particularly for issues related to parameter validation during tool invocation. This client-side interaction leverages [`stdio_client`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L378) and [`ClientSession`](https://github.com/snap-stanford/biomni/biomni/agent/a1.py#L377) for managing the asynchronous communication with the server and executing tool calls. More details on the MCP server setup can be found in [Setting up and Running a Multi-Component Protocol (MCP) Server](#tutorials-and-examples-setting-up-and-running-a-multi-component-protocol-mcp-server).
